item.title: Top Super PAC for Senate Democrats Raises Record $151 Million in Third Quarter
item.description: Democratic Senate candidates have generally out-raised Republicans, but are struggling to match outside spending from Trump-affiliated groups.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: The Senate Majority PAC, which is led by close allies of Senator Chuck Schumer, raised $151 million in the third quarter.

item.title: L.A. Philanthropist Says Suit Over Fire Damage Is a Blow for the People
item.description: Austin Beutner has filed a lawsuit that highlights a central dispute after the 2025 Los Angeles fires: Who pays when a house survives the flames but not the smoke?
item.dc:creator: Rukmini Callimachi and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Ryan Young for The New York Times
item.media:description: Austin Beutner is battling his insurance company to get what he believes he is owed for smoke damage.

item.title: Democratic Effort Aims to Keep 2028 Hopefuls Focused on General Election
item.description: A new polling project called Project 270 will work to focus candidates on voters’ interests in presidential battleground states.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Democratic National Convention in Chicago in 2024.

item.title: Why These 5 Methods Used in Executions Have Stirred Debate
item.description: Tennessee’s unsuccessful attempt to end the life of Christa Pike is spurring more scrutiny over capital punishment techniques, and whether the death penalty should exist at all.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
item.media:credit: South Carolina Department of Corrections, via Associated Press
item.media:description: In a photo provided by the South Carolina Department of Corrections, the state’s death chamber in Columbia, S.C., including the electric chair, right, and a firing squad chair, left.

item.title: Democrats Eyeing the House Face a Conundrum: Rent or Buy?
item.description: With less money than G.O.P., Democrats are torn over where to spend in the final weeks. The party is making its biggest move in years against one of G.O.P.’s biggest blue-district survivors.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Democrats’ hold on the House affects Representative Hakeem Jeffries’s ability to govern his party if he becomes speaker next year.

item.title: Cornell Case Highlights Drop in Resolved Sexual Assault Cases Under Trump
item.description: The administration has shifted its enforcement of a civil rights law from allegations of sexual misconduct to issues like blocking protections for transgender students.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:description: President Trump’s administration has had a minimal response to the allegations of gang rape at Cornell University.

item.title: An Alluring Catch in the Florida Keys Isn’t a Fish. It’s Cocaine.
item.description: Bricks of the drug frequently surface in the waters off the island chain. Despite the risks, some who discover “square grouper,” as they’re known, hang onto them.
item.dc:creator: David Ovalle

item.title: How Alaska’s Fish Became a Defining Issue for the Midterms
item.description: In the battle for an Alaska Senate seat and the governor’s mansion, the oil-dependent state’s declining fisheries loom large, but no one wants to look at the biggest culprit, climate change.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin and Kerry Tasker

item.title: Jim Bakker, Television Preacher Felled by Sex and Financial Scandals, Dies at 86
item.description: With his wife, Tammy Faye, Mr. Bakker built a broadcasting juggernaut around the gospel of prosperity.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Haberman
item.media:description: Jim Bakker in 1987. The television ministry he founded with his first wife, Tammy Faye Bakker, brought in as much as $129 million annually before he was felled by a sex scandal.

item.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Says, ‘If Abdul Can Win in Michigan, Anybody Can Win Anywhere’
item.description: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez made the remarks about Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, as she considers whether to run for president in 2028.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: Democrats are watching closely for hints about whether Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York might run for president or for the Senate in 2028.

item.description: According to U.S. and British officials, 12 B-1 Air Force bombers from R.A.F. Fairford air base were withdrawn because of the risk of a drone attack ordered by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

item.title: Trump Orders Execution by Firing Squad for Gunman in 2009 Fort Hood Shooting
item.description: The Pentagon said that Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan, who carried out the deadliest mass shooting at an American military base, would be executed by firing squad.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan in 2010. During his court-martial, he was convicted after admitting to killing 13 people and wounding dozens of others at Fort Hood in Texas.

item.title: U.S. Citizen Accused of Surveilling Taiwanese Family on China’s Behalf
item.description: The woman, Wanying Zhang, was arrested at the Los Angeles airport on Sunday. She was accused of watching the son of Taiwan’s president in Seattle.
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin, Amy Qin and Vik Jolly
item.media:description: A photo provided by the Federal Bureau of Investigation shows Wanying Zhang being arrested on Sunday in Los Angeles.

item.title: White House Blocked Politico From Air Force One for Trump’s Trip to Nebraska
item.description: The move is the latest round in the fight over presidential access after Mr. Trump declared a ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple

item.title: Caleb Flynn, Who Appeared on ‘American Idol,’ Gets Life Sentence for Wife’s Murder
item.description: Caleb Flynn maintained his innocence at his sentencing hearing in Ohio on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
item.media:description: Caleb Flynn was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole on Monday for fatally shooting his wife, Ashley, in their home in Tipp City, Ohio, in February.

item.title: Judge Sides With Justice Dept. in Dispute Over Subpoena to Times Freelancer
item.description: The magistrate judge’s conclusion is only a recommendation, and a Federal District Court judge is scheduled to hold a hearing on the issue next month.

item.media:description: Investigators are seeking the freelance reporter’s testimony as they seek to identify his sources for an article about a top-secret operation in North Korea.

item.title: Facing Backlash, Trump Says His Super PAC Will Pay for Taxpayer-Funded Ads
item.description: The president said that his PAC, MAGA, Inc., would pay for TV ads promoting him that had been paid for with taxpayer money.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher, Theodore Schleifer and Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: President Trump reversed course and said that his super PAC would pay for ads promoting him, which had been paid for with public funds.

item.title: Chicago Woman Shot by Border Patrol Agent Sues Federal Government
item.description: The lawsuit is the latest in a widening push from people who claim they were harmed by the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown and now want justice.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman

item.title: Biden-Era Memo on Covid and Schools Set Off Dispute in Justice Dept.
item.description: The Trump administration released a report showing career officials had objected to the 2021 memo as evidence that the policy was biased against conservatives. But in an ironic twist, the administration has forced out many of the objectors.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett
item.media:description: Attorney General Merrick B. Garland issued the memo in 2021 to investigate purported threats to schools officials as schools across the country started a third academic year of Covid-related restrictions.

item.title: Hispanic Voters Overwhelmingly Disapprove of Trump, New Poll Shows
item.description: Latino voters, who shifted Republican in the 2024 presidential election, view the party more negatively than they have in the past decade, according to an NBC News/Telemundo poll released on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Soler
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: A polling site in San Antonio, Texas, in May. Movement among Latino voters in Texas as well as Florida could be a key factor in whether control of the Senate changes hands in November.

item.title: 2 People, Including Winter Haven High School Student, Killed in Florida Bus Crash
item.description: A school bus carrying 39 people to Winter Haven High School in Florida was struck by a sedan and rolled over, killing a student and a person in another vehicle, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.category: Winter Haven High School (Winter Haven, Fla)
item.media:description: The bus was hit by a sedan that veered across the center line in Polk County, Fla.

item.title: The Campaign for Ohio’s Next Governor May Be the Ugliest in the Country
item.description: The candidates for Ohio governor have significant policy differences, but the campaign ads have been strikingly personal, with exaggerated portrayals of one candidate as a con artist and the other as a drunk.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson
item.media:credit: Jessica Phelps for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Amy Acton, Ohio’s former chief public health officer, has faced ugly, personal attacks in her run for governor.

item.title: California Prepares to Ban Quartz Countertop Production

item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: A California rule would ban any manufactured stone that contains more than 1 percent of crystalline silica.
